data.gender_notes: Mwenda is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The Swahili name Mwenda translates to 'friend' in English. It is a common name in Swahili-speaking communities, particularly in East Africa. The name Mwenda carries the meaning “Friend” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English. Parents who choose Mwenda usually hope their child will grow to embody friend and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A bond of love and companionship
data.etymology: Mwenda belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Friend.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mwenda total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_greek.name: Μουέντα

in_english.name: Mwenda

in_english.long_meaning: The name Mwenda originates from African roots, specifically in the Swahili language, and it means walking with God or companion of God, in the Christian tradition, this name signifies a close relationship with God, reflecting faith, obedience, and spiritual guidance, and is often associated with qualities like devotion, piety, and righteousness

data.cultural_impact: The name Mwenda holds strong cultural significance in Swahili society due to its emphasis on community, relationships, and friendship. In Swahili culture, kinship and social networks are fundamental to building a strong community and support system. Naming a child Mwenda reflects these values, instilling in the individual a sense of belonging and responsibility to their community.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Mwenda carries deeper meaning. In Christianity, friends are considered to be gifts from God, sent to be companions on our spiritual journey. The name Mwenda can serve as a reminder of the importance of building and nurturing deep spiritual friendships, as well as embodying Christ-like love and compassion towards others. The name encourages the individual to seek out meaningful connections rooted in mutual support, encouragement, and accountability, ultimately reflecting the communal nature of the Christian faith.

modern_usage.modern_context: Mwenda is a common African name, particularly in Uganda. It is derived from the Bantu word 'mwendo', which means 'friend' or 'ally'. In modern usage, the name has gained popularity on social media and personal blogs as a representation of African heritage and unity.
